en.question: A document assistant must parse arbitrary supplier attachments with a native parser. Security policy assumes a malicious attachment might exploit that parser: even then, the parse job must not read host credentials or contact the network. Only extracted text is needed. Which containment design best meets this threat model?

options.text: Run parsing in a rootless worker that mounts the application home directory read-only and shares the application's network access.
options.note: Read-only mounting still permits credential disclosure, and rootless execution does not remove network access. Both resources remain reachable after a parser exploit.

options.text: Run parsing on a separate worker with read-only production credentials and restrict network requests to authenticated HTTPS connections.
options.note: Read-only credentials are still secrets, and authenticated HTTPS can still carry exfiltrated data. A separate host does not satisfy the explicit resource restrictions.

options.text: Run parsing in the trusted application process, then screen and sanitize the extracted text before it enters the model context.
options.note: Text screening occurs after the native parser has processed the attachment. It cannot contain code execution that already occurred in the credential-bearing application process.

options.text: Run parsing in a disposable isolated sandbox with only the attachment mounted, no host secrets, blocked network access, and resource limits.
options.note: The execution environment denies the resources the attacker seeks even if the parser is compromised. Resource limits also contain excessive work without depending on a model's judgment of the attachment.
